text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- Newspaper editorial says the OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky came under fire from President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party for his stand on the rebel committees in the south.
- Humanitarian aid was unloaded in Durres port as more equipment arrived for the French troops of the multinational protection force.
- Greece has stopped supplying fuel to Albania, according to the local authorities in the south eastern towns of Korce and Devoll.
- Tirana police were surprised by an impromptu rally of some 20 youths demanding Vranitzky be neutral.

- The small centre-right Democratic Alliance party alleges the National Council of Defence headed by Berisha planned to wipe out opposition in the south with military force. The salvation committees should be considered as a party in the talks, it says.
- Besides Sude all the other arrested managers of the failed pyramid investment schemes have not returned to prison.
- The Interior Ministry has sent special forces to restore order in the northern town of Shkoder.
- Schools and universities are to resume lessons by April 28th, according to the two education ministries covering them.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- The failed pyramid investment schemes have taken away about half of Albania's GDP, or $1.2 billion, according to Finance Minister Arben Malaj.
- United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan said no foreign troops would attempt to gather weapons from the Albanian population.
- Political parties told the Prime Minister Bashkim Fino they want a proportional representation in the general elections.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Authorities of town halls and communes will decide if schools are to be reopened by April 21.
In a telephone conversation Turkish President Suleyman Demirel told his Albanian counterpart Sali Berisha Turkey would send assistance to Albania to overcome the crisis.
- U.S.-Hungarian financier George Soros funded Koha Jone daily, which was a key factor in sparking anti-government protests in the south of the country, a newspaper commentary says.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- Socialist leader Fatos Nano says democratisation should continue because it is the only way to help the country out of the crisis and prepare the general elections which will save Albania.
